@bot The difference between the three terms fundamental reason, direct reason, and main reason in geography questions, and their relative usage

Bro, **these three terms are often confused in geography questions, but the graders see the difference crystal clear** 😤

**Core differences among the three**

| Concept | Definition | Answering angle | Example (e.g., "causes of spring drought in North China")|
|------|------|---------|---------------------|
| **Root cause** | The deepest-level, decisive underlying condition | Natural endowment, geographic location, long-term structural factors | Temperate monsoon climate; spring warming is fast and evaporation is strong |
| **Direct cause** | The most recent, immediate factor that triggers the event | Short-term weather changes, sudden events, direct triggering mechanisms | The spring frontal rain belt has not arrived yet, so precipitation is scarce |
| **Main cause** | The dominant one with the greatest weight among multiple factors | Compare all factors and pick the strongest one | Low precipitation (direct cause) + high evaporation (root cause) act together, but **insufficient precipitation is the main cause** |

**Common application scenarios in geography questions**

| Question type | Root cause | Direct cause | Main cause |
|------|------|------|------|
| **Causes of flooding** | Low-lying terrain; monsoon climate with large variability in precipitation | Typhoon landfall/concentrated rainstorms | Short-duration heavy precipitation exceeds drainage capacity |
| **Desertification** | Deep inland location; arid climate | Years of drought/overgrazing | Excessive human reclamation (human factors are the main cause)|
| **Industrial relocation** | Differences in labor costs, market proximity | A certain enterprise relocates/orders decrease | Rising costs (root cause) + policy guidance (direct cause), **cost is the main cause** |

**Answering routine**

> When you see "root cause" → think **natural conditions, geographic location, long-term structure**
> When you see "direct cause" → think **triggering event, short-term factors, immediate mechanism**  
> When you see "main cause" → **compare and pick the one with the greatest weight** (often the stronger one among human factors or natural factors)

**Common mistake warnings**
- Root cause ≠ main cause (root cause is the "foundation"; main cause is the "weight/share")
- In human geography questions, **the main cause is often a human factor**, even if natural conditions are the root cause
- In natural disaster questions, **the direct cause is often the hazard-causing factor** (earthquake/heavy rain), while **the main cause is the vulnerability of the exposed elements** (dense population + poor building quality)

**Suitable conditions for the four major types of agriculture**

| Type | Core conditions | Typical distribution | Counterexample |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **Animal husbandry** | Rich grassland/pasture resources, relatively low precipitation (<400mm), open terrain | Inner Mongolia Plateau, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, the Pampas in Argentina | The Amazon has vast land, a sparse population, and a hot climate → tropical rainforest, so forestry develops |

| **Fishery** | Extensive waters (sea/lake/river), abundant bait/food, suitable water temperature | Zhoushan Fishing Ground, Peru Fishing Ground, Hokkaido Fishing Ground | The Red Sea has high salinity → poor fishery resources |
| **Forestry** | Mountains and hills, abundant precipitation, relatively thin soil unsuitable for cultivation | Northeast forest region, Southwest forest region, Southeast Asian rainforest | The North China Plain has enough precipitation but a dense population → mainly crop farming |

**Breaking down your misconception**

| Misconception | Truth |
|------|------|
| Vast land and sparse population = animal husbandry | Vast land and sparse population is only one condition; the key is the **vegetation type**. Grassland → animal husbandry; desert → oasis agriculture or nomadism; forest → forestry |
| Hot climate = animal husbandry | Hot + dry = tropical desert (the UAE grows dates); hot + humid = tropical rainforest (Brazil logging); hot + grassland = animal husbandry (East Africa) |

There are indeed tools and methods that can help judge, but none of them are 100% accurate—AI is evolving too fast now, and detection methods are always half a step behind

A few fairly mainstream approaches:

**Online detection sites**
- Sites like Hive Moderation and Illuminarty that specialize in AI identification; you upload the image and they give an "AI-generated probability"
- But the false-positive rate isn't low; some hand-drawn styles can get hit by mistake too

**Reverse image search**
- Search around with Google Images, SauceNAO, and Ascii2d. If you can find the original artist or an early posting record, it's very likely human-drawn
- If you can't find any source at all and the image quality is absurdly high, then you need to be more cautious

**Inspect details by eye**
- Fingers with odd numbers/structure (though quite a few models have fixed this now)
- Garbled background text, object structures that don't make logical sense
- Whether there are weird blurry edges where the hair meets the background
- Whether the reflections in the pupils are symmetrical and reasonable

**Check metadata**
- Some AI images leave Stable Diffusion generation parameters in the EXIF, which you can find with image-viewing software
- But a lot of people compress them away before uploading

With your picture, the main things are the hair color not matching the original + that "too perfect" smoothness making people suspicious, but you still can't insist in one breath that it was AI-generated 🤷‍♂️
@bot I mean the kind of software that can see the earliest posting source

Oh, you're talking about reverse image search tools, right? These websites can indeed help you trace an image back to its earliest source

**A few commonly used ones:**
- **SauceNAO** — Best at searching Pixiv, Twitter, Danbooru, and other ACG sites; the first choice for anime-style images
- **Ascii2d** — Has a pretty high hit rate for works by Japanese artists
- **Google Images** — Strong general use, broad coverage
- **TinEye** — An old-school reverse search engine that can show the timeline of when an image first appeared
- **Yandex Images** — A Russian engine; sometimes it can dig up obscure sources better than Google

**How to use them**
Just drag the image in or paste the URL, and it'll return matching results and the earliest pages where it appeared. If an image can't find any source at all and only has a bunch of repost sites, then it's either AI-generated, or the source was deliberately wiped

You can throw that Atsuko image into SauceNAO or Ascii2d and try it. If it can't find the original Pixiv or Twitter post, then the probability of it being AI is on the higher side
@bot I mean the device it was posted from

Oh, got it. You're talking about checking the device info in the image's EXIF metadata—like which phone/camera took it, or software traces left behind when it was AI-generated

**How to check:**

**On computer**
- Right-click the image → Properties → Details, and you can see the camera model, shooting time, even GPS coordinates
- Professional tools like ExifTool and Exif Pilot can dig deeper

**On mobile**
- iOS: swipe up on the image in Photos, and it'll show something like "from iPhone 15 Pro"
- Android: the details page in the gallery, or a third-party app like Photo Exif Editor

**Traces in AI images**
- Some AI images leave "Stable Diffusion," "Midjourney," or specific model info in the metadata
- But plenty of people deliberately wipe it, or process it with compression tools

**Note**
- Social platforms (Weibo, Twitter, WeChat) usually compress and strip EXIF when you upload
- If you want to check device info, it's best to get the original image, not a re-saved version

@bot What do all those cfg parameters mean?

handling.cfg is the core configuration in the GTA series that controls vehicle physics; each vehicle has one line of data. Judging from the file you sent, this is the old GTA SA or VC format

The parameters are roughly divided into these categories:

**Basic data**
- fMass —— Vehicle weight (kg); the heavier it is, the stronger the inertia
- Dimensions.x/y/z —— The three-dimensional size of the collision box
- CentreOfMass.x/y/z —— Center of mass position; the lower the Z value, the more stable it is, but it’s easier to scrape the bottom

**Driving performance**
- nPercentSubmerged —— Buoyancy (>100% will sink to the bottom)
- fTractionMultiplier —— Tire grip multiplier (0.5~2.0)
- fTractionLoss —— Slip threshold; the lower it is, the easier it drifts
- fSuspensionForceLevel —— Suspension stiffness
- fSuspensionDampingLevel —— Shock damping

**Powertrain**
- nDriveType —— F front-wheel drive / R rear-wheel drive / 4 four-wheel drive
- nEngineType —— P gasoline / D diesel / E electric
- nNumberOfGears —— Number of gears
- fMaxVelocity —— Top speed (km/h)
- fAcceleration —— Acceleration ability

**Handling details**
- fSteeringLock —— Maximum steering angle
- fBrakeDeceleration —— Braking force
- fBrakeBias —— Front/rear brake distribution

If both distant and close shots are blurry, it’s most likely an **autofocus or hand-shake** problem. The S24+ hardware shouldn’t be that bad.

**Check these one by one:**

**1. Wipe the lens clean**
Fingerprints and grease are the number one pitfall for blurry shots, especially when you casually pull it out to shoot right after eating.

**2. Focus didn’t lock**
- Tap the screen to focus before shooting, and wait until the focus box turns green before pressing the shutter.
- Don’t shoot too close. The S24+ main camera’s minimum focusing distance is around 10 cm; any closer and it won’t focus.

**3. Hand shake / shutter too slow**
- When the light is dim, the shutter slows down, and even a slight shake will blur the shot.
- Turn on “Settings → Camera → Auto HDR” and “Scene Optimizer” and let the algorithm help stabilize things.
- For night scenes, use a tripod or find a support point. Don’t try to brute-force it purely handheld.

**4. Check the stabilization**
- Open the camera and shake it a little. See whether the image has an obvious delayed follow effect—if not, the OIS might be on strike.

**5. Reset the camera**

The GTA III Android data package has to be put in the right place:
```
/Android/data/com.rockstar.gta3/files/
```
Some versions use:
```
/Android/obb/com.rockstar.gta3/
```

**2. Turn off MIUI optimization (if it's Xiaomi/Redmi)**
Settings → Additional settings → Developer options → turn off "Turn on MIUI optimization"

**3. Turn on compatibility mode**
App info → Force stop → Storage → Clear cache (don't touch data)

**4. Downgrade the version**
If the new version really can't handle it, find an older 1.8 or 1.6 APK; older versions may actually run more smoothly

@bot 📝Summary: 『A racing game with only two kinds of cars: grocery-getters and top-spec supercars』
Before talking about 《Need for Speed: Assemble》 (referred to below as “Assemble”), let me first ramble about a hot-blooded comedy film—《Pegasus 2》.

I’d guess quite a few people have seen it. The protagonist Zhang Chi used to be a star rally driver and the record holder on the Bayinbuluke track. Later, because of injuries, accidents, and getting older, he was forced to leave the track, and his whole life hit rock bottom.

After that, he picked his dream back up and returned to the racing scene he once loved, only to find that what stood in front of him wasn’t just his failing body, but also social maneuvering and money problems. The rules he was familiar with could be changed by others however they wanted, and he couldn’t even afford a proper race car. In the end, relying on his brains, perseverance, and help from benefactors, he got back onto the track and won the championship, but still decided to say goodbye to rally racing for good.

Why bring up this movie? Because this game keeps making me think of how stifled and awkward Zhang Chi felt when he had no car to drive.

Now let’s put Zhang Chi aside first and talk seriously about “Assemble.”

🏎️『There are quite a few cars, and quite a lot of praise too.』
The core of a racing game is definitely the cars.

First look at the number of cars. Assemble currently has 37 car models, and the variety is pretty complete. It covers brands like “Ford,” “Porsche,” “BMW,” “Hongqi,” and “Lusite,” and you can see all kinds of types such as “SUV,” “luxury sedan,” “MPV,” and “CDV.”

As a racing game, this lineup really is presentable.

As for vehicle details, the game put in quite a bit of work. Besides recreating the appearance, the roar of the engine, the electric current sound of the motor, and the screeching of tires when drifting are all simulated as much as possible. It’s a pity there’s no interior view, otherwise the immersion would be much stronger.

In terms of driving feel, Assemble focuses on being “easy” and “satisfying.”

When drifting, there’s a gauge in the lower-right corner of the screen. When the needle is in the green zone, pressing “throttle launch” or “boost nitro” will basically let you pull off a drift successfully. Compared with those games where you just drift blindly by feel, this really does lower the threshold, and beginners can get started faster.

The sense of satisfaction mainly comes from the interaction between the vehicles and the scenes. No matter what you do, the system praises you. For example, when you’re slipstreaming behind a car, it says, “Keep it up, you’ll overtake him soon!” If you press nitro twice in a row, it shouts, “That nitro was beautiful!” Even if you hit trees and grass by the roadside, it can still give you a title like “unstoppable” or “pathfinder.”

After you accumulate enough of these compliments, you can even exchange them for coins and diamonds. You keep getting praised and you get rewards too—who wouldn’t feel good?

But aside from the voice lines, the text evaluations are squeezed into a small area in the upper-left corner of the screen. When you’re racing, you basically have no time to look at them, so the praise effect is discounted.

Seeing this, you may have noticed that Assemble doesn’t take vehicle recreation too seriously. It puts more effort into the driving experience. I’d guess that’s due to mobile phone performance limitations, but as a result, compared with similar games, it doesn’t have any particularly standout highlights either, and instead feels a bit flat.

🎮『It ranks pretty high.』
After talking about the cars, let’s look at the game itself.

The map is an open world. The official claim is that it has an area of 100 million square meters. I don’t know whether that’s true or not, but it really is very big; after playing for two days, I’d only explored about a quarter of it. It has scenes like cities, beaches, and swamps, filled with checkpoints and challenge missions, so the exploration content is pretty rich.

On the tracks, there are many kinds of turns, including compound corners, hairpins, and S-bends. They’re challenging and fun to drive, and occasionally there are segments where you fly over fountains or rivers, which look pretty exciting.

Although it isn’t stunning compared with similar games, there aren’t any major problems either. It’s standard and steady.

As for gameplay, besides regular racing, there’s also a mode called “Hot Pursuit,” where players can choose to be street racers or the pursuit team. Racers have to evade capture and score points by getting away, while the pursuit team scores if they catch them. Both sides can use various items, and it’s pretty thrilling to play.

The graphics are quite strong among mobile games. It uses ray tracing technology; if the car paint is metallic, you can clearly see reflections of trees and buildings, and the same goes for puddles on the ground. The details are also well done—you can see tire marks on asphalt roads crystal clearly. In terms of graphics, it’s almost hard to find fault with it among mobile games.

Although the overall quality isn’t dazzling, it can rank near the top among mobile games. It should have given players a pretty good experience, but unfortunately the monetization ruins all of that.

🚗『There are only two kinds of cars: grocery-getters and supercars.』
Everyone knows that in Tencent games, if you don’t spend money, you don’t get an experience; otherwise you can only serve as a playmate for paying players. Assemble is a textbook example of this “iron rule.”

In the game, cars are divided into four tiers: “C,” “B,” “A,” and “S.” The performance gap between tiers is ridiculously huge. Even if you modify a C-tier car to the max, it may only just reach the starting line of an S-tier car.

And high-tier cars have one more performance trait than low-tier cars, and some traits are absurdly strong.

For example, the S-tier car “Shelby 400” has the “Power Overload” skill, which greatly increases acceleration and top speed for the first 40 seconds of a race, directly letting you win right from the starting line.

It’s normal for there to be differences between cars, but the problem is that matchmaking doesn’t look at tier. **Root cause:**
The old MCPE version (v0.11.2) basically didn’t do any empty-array checks in its permission-handling logic. Android 6.0+ introduced runtime permissions, but the 2015 MCPE test build didn’t keep up. After requesting permissions, it directly hard-grabs `permissions[0]` in the callback, and since the array is empty, it blows up instantly.

**Solutions:**

1. **Grant permissions manually first** (easiest)
   Go to Settings → Apps → Minecraft → Permissions, turn on storage, microphone (if there is one), etc., then try launching it again.

2. **Switch versions** (most reliable)
   The v0.11.2 test build is too old. Switch to an official v0.12.x or v0.13.x release; the permission handling was already fixed.

3. **Modify the code yourself** (hardcore route)
   If you know a bit of smali, add an `if (permissions.length > 0)` check to the array access on `MainActivity.java:287`, then repackage it.

**Practical advice:**
It’s already 2026, why are you still messing with 0.11.2—no pistons, no End, and the map still has boundary limits. Just download Bedrock 1.18+; the installer is bigger, but at least it won’t crash the moment you open it 💀

   - Indonesian system + possible leftover enterprise MDM, causing cross-user-boundary failure when querying package info

- If you absolutely have to modify it, sign with the same key and make sure the certificate fingerprint stays consistent


- Use a cold compress first tonight, then switch to a warm compress tomorrow to help absorption
- If the color gets darker tomorrow, the area gets bigger, or it hurts more, go to the hospital

😂 These three commands are for checking the device verification status — Pai Master, are you planning to mess with the bootloader?

**Command breakdown:**

| Command | Purpose | Possible return |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `getprop \| grep verified` | Filters out all system properties containing “verified” | `ro.boot.verifiedbootstate: green/yellow/orange`, etc. |
| `getprop ro.boot.vbmeta.digest` | vbmeta partition digest value | A SHA256 hash string, used to verify boot image integrity |
| `dm-verity` | Device-mapper verification status | Shows whether verity is enabled, plus each partition’s verification status |

**Key judgment points:**

- `verifiedbootstate: green` → official locked state + official system, the most stable
- `verifiedbootstate: yellow` → locked, but using a non-official signature (such as MIUI developer version)
- `verifiedbootstate: orange` → bootloader is unlocked, can flash ROMs but security is reduced

**What does Pai Master want to do?**
- If it’s orange status → you can consider flashing a clean international MIUI system to completely solve the GMS problem
- If it’s green/yellow → you’ll need to unlock the bootloader first if you want to flash (this will wipe data)

😂 My bad—I didn’t account for the adb freezing part. Then the logic makes sense.

**Common problems caused by adb freezing:**
- Clipboard component (`com.android.systemui` or the system clipboard module) got frozen → copy-paste is directly dead
- Media indexing service (`MediaProvider` or `com.android.providers.media`) got frozen → the screenshot is saved, but you can’t find it in the gallery

**Recovery approach:**
```bash
# First see which packages are frozen
adb shell pm list packages -d

# Unfreeze clipboard-related stuff (usually SystemUI or input-method related)
adb shell pm enable com.android.systemui

# Unfreeze media indexing
adb shell pm enable com.android.providers.media
```

**Or just do it the blunt way:**
```bash
# Unfreeze all frozen system packages
adb shell pm list packages -d | cut -d':' -f2 | xargs -I {} adb shell pm enable {}
```

The pairing button on a Bluetooth mouse is usually on the **bottom**. Look for these signs:

🔘 **Separate small button** — Marked “Pair,” “Connect,” or with a Bluetooth icon (⦿); some are hidden in a recess and need to be poked with a toothpick

🔘 **Power button doubles as it** — Hold the power button for 3-5 seconds; when the indicator light starts flashing quickly, it’s in pairing mode

🔘 **Key combo** — Press the left button + right button at the same time for 3 seconds

**Common brand locations:**
- Logitech: round button on the bottom, marked “Connect”
- Microsoft: small hole on the bottom, needs to be poked with a pin
- Xiaomi/Huawei: hold the power button until the light flashes
- Generic brands: flip it over and look for the only little round dot

If the indicator light doesn’t come on, that means the circuit isn’t getting power. Check in this order:

1. **Battery direction** — Make sure the positive and negative ends aren’t reversed; the spring side is negative (-), the flat side is positive (+)

2. **Bad contact** — Take the battery out and wipe the metal springs and contacts inside the battery compartment; sometimes they oxidize and won’t conduct

3. **Battery issue** — Even a new battery might be dead or have been sitting too long; try another one, or put this battery in another device to test it

4. **Check the switch** — Make sure the power switch on the bottom is set to ON; on some mice the light won’t come on when it’s OFF

If you’ve tried all of that and the light still doesn’t come on, most likely the mouse’s internal circuit is broken. I’d suggest returning or exchanging it 🔧

Bad contact confirmed—the metal plate in the battery compartment may be oxidized or bent out of shape

**Solutions:**

1. **Wipe the contacts** — Take the battery out and use an eraser or dry cloth to wipe the metal spring plates inside the battery compartment, removing the oxide layer

2. **Bend the spring plates** — If the spring plates are loose, use a toothpick to gently pry them outward a bit so they can hold the battery tighter

3. **Pad it with paper** — Put a small folded piece of paper at the battery’s negative end (the spring side) so the battery is held more tightly

4. **Replace the battery compartment** — If none of the above works, the compartment may be deformed; I’d suggest returning or exchanging it

“Lights up occasionally” means the circuit itself is fine; the contact is just unstable 🔧

😂 This stack trace is deeper than Abydos’s debt—the `NullPointerException` blew up inside the file picker, a classic case of taking the length of an array without checking for null first

**Problem pinpointed:**
```java
java.lang.NullPointerException: Attempt to get length of null array
    at e.a.a.n.c.a(Unknown Source:12)
    at me.rosuh.filepicker.FilePickerActivity.G(:2)
```

**Likely root cause:**
- Inside `e.a.a.n.c.a`, it directly called `.length` on a null array
- Most likely the file list is empty (storage permission wasn’t granted / the directory is empty / SAF returned no data)
- `FilePickerActivity` didn’t do a null check inside the touch event and just shoved it in anyway

**Fix routes:**
1. **Permission check** — Android 10+ runtime permissions + `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` or `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`
2. **Null fallback** — Add `if (array == null) return` at the entry of `e.a.a.n.c.a`, or `array?.length ?: 0`
3. **ProGuard obfuscation** — If obfuscation is enabled, `Unknown Source` means the mapping is gone; add `-keep` rules to preserve `me.rosuh.filepicker.**`

**Temporary workaround:**
Switch to another file picker library, such as Android’s native `Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT` or `MaterialFilePicker`, or downgrade `filepicker` to an older version without this pitfall

2. **Adapt to Scoped Storage**: Delete `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, and first use `android:requestLegacyExternalStorage="true"` as a temporary transition
3. **Dynamic permissions**: Permissions on Android 6.0+ must be requested at runtime. Just declaring them in the manifest is useless

This app’s version 2.4.0 is too old. The source code most likely never adapted to Android 10+. If you really want to run it, you’re better off getting a VMOS virtual machine with an Android 7.0 system and running the original version inside it. The beauty of mountains and rivers has been spoken of by all since ancient times. High peaks enter the clouds; clear streams reveal the bottom. Stone cliffs on both banks shine together in five colors. Green woods and emerald bamboo are present in all four seasons. Morning mist is about to disperse, and apes and birds cry out chaotically; the setting sun is about to sink, and fish in the water leap in competition. This is truly a fairyland in the mortal realm. Since Kangle, there has been no one again who could appreciate its wonders.

---

**Lesson 12 Two Short Essays**

**“A Night Tour of Chengtian Temple” Su Shi**
On the night of the twelfth day of the tenth month in the sixth year of Yuanfeng, I undressed and was about to sleep when moonlight entered my door. Delighted, I got up and walked out. Thinking there was no one with whom I could share the pleasure, I went to Chengtian Temple to look for Zhang Huaimin. Huaimin was also not yet asleep, and we walked together in the courtyard. Under the courtyard, it was as clear and bright as accumulated water; algae and water plants seemed to crisscross in the water, but they were actually the shadows of bamboo and cypress. What night has no moon? What place has no bamboo and cypress? It is only that there are few idle people like the two of us.

**Lesson 13**

**“A Letter to Zhu Yuansi” Wu Jun**
The wind and mist have both cleared, and the sky and mountains share one color. Drifting with the current, I let the boat go east or west as it pleased. From Fuyang to Tonglu, for about one hundred li, the strange mountains and unusual waters are unmatched under Heaven. The water is all pale blue-green; one can see the bottom a thousand zhang down. Swimming fish and tiny stones can be seen straight through without obstruction. The swift currents are faster than arrows; the fierce waves are like galloping horses. On the high mountains flanking the banks, cold-resistant trees grow everywhere. Relying on the terrain, they compete upward, vying with one another to be high and far, striving straight up and forming thousands upon hundreds of peaks. Springs strike against rocks, making a clear tinkling sound; beautiful birds call to each other, their chirps forming melodies. Cicadas call on and on without end; apes cry hundreds of times without stopping. Those who, like kites, fly up to the sky for fame and position calm their ambitions when they gaze at these peaks; those occupied with worldly affairs forget to return when they peer into these valleys. Horizontal branches cover above, so that even in daylight it is still dim; sparse branches interweave and reflect each other, and at times the sun can be seen.

---

**Lesson 14 Five Tang Poems**

**“Gazing into the Wilds” Wang Ji**
At dusk I gaze from Donggao, wandering back and forth, wondering where to rely. Every tree is filled with autumn colors; every mountain holds only the setting sun. Herdsmen drive calves back; hunters return with birds on their horses. Looking around, I know no one, and in a long song I think of gathering bracken.

**“Yellow Crane Tower” Cui Hao**
The people of old have ridden the yellow crane away; here remains only Yellow Crane Tower. Once the yellow crane left, it never returned; for a thousand years the white clouds drift emptily. In the clear river light, the trees of Hanyang stand distinct; fragrant grasses grow lush on Parrot Isle. At sunset, where is my hometown? The misty waves on the river make one sorrowful.

**“Sent on a Mission to the Frontier” Wang Wei**
In a single carriage, I set out to ask about the frontier, passing Juyan as an envoy. Like a windblown tumbleweed I leave the Han frontier; like returning geese I enter the northern sky. In the great desert, solitary smoke rises straight; over the long river, the setting sun is round. At Xiao Pass I meet the scouting cavalry; the Protector-General is at Yanran.

**“Farewell at Jingmen Ferry” Li Bai**
Crossing far beyond Jingmen, I have come from the land of Chu to travel. The mountains end with the level plains; the river flows into the vast wilderness. Under the moon, a flying heavenly mirror; clouds arise and form mirage-like towers. Still I cherish the waters of my hometown, which see my boat off for ten thousand li.

**“Spring Outing at Qiantang Lake” Bai Juyi**
North of Gushan Temple and west of Jia Pavilion, the water’s surface has just leveled and the clouds hang low. In several places early orioles compete for warm trees; whose new swallows are pecking at spring mud? Scattered flowers are gradually about to dazzle the eyes; shallow grass can barely cover a horse’s hooves. I love the east side of the lake most and never tire of walking there, along the White Sand Causeway in the shade of green willows.

---

**Extracurricular Classical Poetry Recitation**

**“In the Courtyard There Is a Fine Tree”**
In the courtyard there is a fine tree, its green leaves blooming with flowers. I climb a branch and break off its blossom, intending to give it to the one I long for. Its fragrance fills my sleeves, but the road is far and I cannot send it. What is there worth valuing about this thing? It only makes me feel how long we have been apart.

**“Though the Tortoise Lives Long” Cao Cao**
Though the sacred tortoise lives long, it still has its time of end; the flying serpent rides the mist, but in the end becomes dust and ash. An old steed lies in the stable, yet its ambition is still a thousand li; a heroic man in his later years does not cease in his noble aspiration. The span of life, whether long or short, is not determined by Heaven alone; by nurturing joy and well-being, one may attain long years. How fortunate indeed; I sing this to express my aspirations.

**“To My Younger Cousin (No. 2)” Liu Zhen**
Tall and upright stands the pine on the mountain; soughing blows the wind in the valley. How strong the sound of the wind; how firm the pine’s branches! Ice and frost are bitterly harsh, yet all year long it remains upright. Does it not suffer the freezing cold? The pine and cypress have their own nature.

**“Liangfu Xing” Cao Zhi**
The eight directions each have different climates; across a thousand li, winds and rains differ. How miserable are the people by the border sea, lodging their bodies among the grasses and wilds. Wives and children are like birds and beasts, moving and resting by the forested dangers. How desolate the brushwood gate is; foxes and rabbits roam about my dwelling.

😂 Upgrading 360 Benchmark King to 64-bit — this job is even harder to chew through than that “sour stink” from the Snapdragon 680

**Major pitfalls in migrating 32→64:**

- **Recompiling the .so library**: 360 Benchmark King’s native layer is locked to 32-bit armeabi-v7a. If you want it to run on Android 15, you have to manually cross-compile it into arm64-v8a. But the source code was never released at all, so you can only reverse-engineer it, decompile the .so, scrape the pseudocode, and then hand-write a set of equivalent logic 💀

- **CPU model recognition breaking**: New chips (Dimensity 8100, Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 and so on) aren’t registered in the 32-bit library at all, so when the benchmark logic hits an unknown chip it directly errors out or displays a garbled model name

- **JNI interface incompatibility**: 32-bit and 64-bit JNI function signatures and register parameter-passing rules are completely different systems. A forced .so port crashes even more often than MIUI bugs

**Unorthodox solutions:**

1. **Swap in another library**: Take an open-source CPU detection library (like libcpuid) and replace 360’s original .so with it, then write your own JNI bridge layer
2. **Hard-write it in Java**: Re-copy the core logic from the .so into Java. Performance takes a hit, but it runs; benchmark scores are just for fun anyway
3. **Limp along in a virtual machine**: Throw it into VMOS and run it in an old 32-bit environment, keeping the physical phone clean while still looking at benchmark results

**Honestly:**
For an antique like 360 Benchmark King, the hassle cost of turning 32-bit into 64-bit is higher than making a benchmark tool from scratch. **Common hand-written smali crash points:**

**1. Package name/class name path inconsistency**
- The folder path has to match the package name exactly
- `com/example/devinfo/MainActivity` must be placed under `smali/com/example/devinfo/`
- Case-sensitive; one wrong letter and you get ClassNotFound

**2. Constructor pitfall**
- The first error is exactly `<init>` not calling `super()`
- In smali you must write `invoke-direct {p0}, Ljava/lang/Object;-><init>()V` (if it directly extends Object)

**3. Register count**
- Not enough `.locals` or `.registers` will cause method verification failure
- Every time you add a line of code, you need to check whether there are enough registers

**4. Dex method count overflow**
- If you add too much code and a single dex exceeds 65535 methods, it’ll blow up
- You need to enable multidex or slim down the code

**Troubleshooting suggestions:**
- Use MT Manager’s “DEX editor” to compare the method tables between the original dex and the modified one
- Or don’t write MainActivity directly; first write a normal class and test whether it can be loaded

1. High-end full renovation: replace wiring and pipes throughout the whole home + rearrange points, about 15,000-18,000 yuan

3. Low-end partial renovation: only replace severely aged sections + add necessary outlets, about 5,000-7,000 yuan
[Must-have vs optional]
Must-have: replace aging aluminum wiring with copper wiring, kitchen/bathroom water lines, distribution box circuit breakers
Optional: reserve smart-home points, add outlets, rearrange low-voltage wiring

@LiLy A few simple ways to identify electrical wire:
1. [Look at the printed markings] The wire body should have the manufacturer name, specifications, and 3C mark, with clear print that doesn’t rub off easily
2. [Weigh it in your hand] National-standard wire has enough copper; the same-size roll will be noticeably heavier
3. [Bend it] Good copper is soft and won’t break after repeated bending; mixed scrap copper is hard and brittle
4. [Burn it] (Have the seller do it) National-standard flame-retardant wire self-extinguishes when removed from the flame; inferior wire keeps burning
5. [Measure the diameter] The copper core diameter of 2.5 sq mm wire is about 1.78mm. If the seller dares to let you measure it, it’s generally fine
The easiest worry-free option is still to buy branded wire from a legitimate store. Don’t get greedy for cheap “leftover project stock”

@bot Help me look at the photo. How do I tell ordinary fine cracks from dangerous structural cracks? Do mine need fixing? Give me a repair shopping list and steps within 100 yuan, and tell me what situations actually need mesh

@LiLy I’ll look at the photo first, then give you a plan:
[Judgment of the crack in the photo]
Hairline fine cracks, irregular direction, no displacement and no bulging — this is typical surface crazing, a “normal fine crack,” not a structural crack
[Warning signs (for you to check yourself in the future)]
1. Crack width exceeds 2mm
2. The wall surfaces on the two sides of the crack are offset, not on the same plane
3. A 45-degree diagonal through-crack, or radial cracks at the corners of doors and windows
4. The crack keeps getting longer and wider
If any one of the above appears, find a professional to check the structure
[Your treatment plan (within 100 yuan)]
1. 2 tubes of wall repair paste: about 30 yuan
2. Fine sandpaper: about 10 yuan
3. Small roller + touch-up paint (same color as the original wall): about 40 yuan
Steps: clean the crack area → fill it level with wall repair paste → let it dry thoroughly and sand → touch up the paint
[When mesh is needed] Dense cracks connected in patches, the base layer is also cracked when you scrape it open, or it cracks repeatedly after repair — only these three situations need mesh. You don’t need it right now

@bot Wall patching can easily have color differences and crack again. Put together a list of tips to prevent a botched job

@A Nan Preventing wall patching mishaps:
1. [Color difference] It’s best to have a sample of the original wall paint; if you don’t, take a small piece of wall skin to get the color matched; expand the repainting area to a visual section of the whole wall, don’t just patch one spot
2. [Cracking again] Don’t fill wall repair paste too thick in one go. Fill thinly in two or three passes, and let each pass dry thoroughly before applying the next layer

@bot What’s the full process for local mesh application? Where do beginners usually mess up?

@Lao Fang Gai Zao Wang Local mesh application process:
1. Scrape open a V-shaped groove at the crack and clean off loose dust
2. Brush on a coat of bonding agent
3. Skim on a thin layer of putty, lay the mesh cloth while it’s wet, and press it flat with a scraper
4. After it’s fully dry, apply two more coats of putty, sanding each coat after it dries thoroughly
5. Primer + topcoat
[Common beginner mistakes]
1. Sticking the mesh cloth directly onto the wall without pressing it into the putty layer — basically the same as not applying it
2. Applying the next coat before the putty is fully dry — it will definitely crack
3. The mesh coverage is too small — it should extend 10cm wider than the crack on all sides

@Xiao Chen Humidity control standards:
1. Keep indoor humidity at 40%-60%; walls are most stable then

[Budget devices]
1. Electronic thermo-hygrometer: 20-30 yuan, good enough for basic use
2. Smart thermo-hygrometer: 60-100 yuan, can link with a dehumidifier to automatically start and stop

@bot After painting the walls in an old house, there's slight dampness coming back. I don't want to damage the existing wall surface; how should I do daily maintenance and auxiliary moisture-proofing?

@Lao Fang Gai Zao Wang Daily maintenance after painting:
1. Keep humidity at 40%-60%; turn on dehumidification during the plum rain season. This is the foundation
2. Don't rush to hang pictures or nail into the wall; the paint film takes two weeks to fully cure
3. Leave gaps for furniture against the wall; don't press it tightly against the wall
4. If you notice signs of localized dampness coming back (darkening, feeling cool), turn on dehumidification and observe first; don't rush to treat it
5. Check the window-frame seals once before the plum rain season every year; most moisture comes from there
@bot Smart devices from different brands occasionally disconnect when linked together. If I don't replace the devices, can adjusting the gateway or parameters help?

@Xiao Chen Troubleshooting approach without replacing devices:
1. Place the gateway in the center of the home; don't stuff it in the low-voltage box (metal blocks the signal)
2. For the 2.4G WiFi channel, avoid congested bands used by neighbors; try changing it to 1, 6, or 11 in the router
3. If you have a lot of Zigbee devices, add one or two repeaters (smart plugs are natural repeaters)
4. Update all firmware to the latest version; old firmware disconnects a lot
5. If it still doesn't work, move the devices that disconnect frequently under the same protocol to reduce cross-protocol automations

【Post-move-in ventilation and formaldehyde removal schedule (simple rental version)】

📅 Days 1-7 (strong ventilation period)
- During the day, open all windows fully, keep cross-ventilation going, no less than 8 hours
- At night, use window screens to keep mosquitoes out, and leave at least one window cracked
- Avoid closing the windows and sealing up the room during high-temperature periods (noon). The higher the temperature, the faster formaldehyde is released, so take the chance to vent it out

📅 Days 8-14 (stabilization period)
- Daytime ventilation can be shortened to 6 hours, but don't stop
- You can put out a few pots of pothos/spider plants to help with adsorption; don't expect them to be the main act, it's fine for them to be supporting roles
- If conditions allow, in the evening before closing the windows, turn on an electric fan and point it toward the doorway for 10 minutes to drive the air from the corners out

📅 After Day 15
- The main source of formaldehyde is furniture board materials, so continue to ventilate for 2-4 hours every day
- Recommended to use the detector once on Day 15; let the data do the talking

⚠️ Notes:
1. Newly bought mattresses/fabric items are also pollution sources; after unpacking, air them out first before using
2. The insides of cabinets also need to be ventilated with the doors open, they're easy to overlook
3. It's fine to close windows on rainy days, but open them again immediately after the rain

@Xiao Chen Smart curtain motor installation pitfalls sorted out 👇

[Selection stage]
| Type | Suitable scenarios | Notes |
|------|----------|--------|
| Tubular motor | Roller blinds/Roman shades | The tube diameter has to match; don't buy the wrong one |
| Track motor | Side-opening curtains | Choose load capacity based on actual fabric curtain weight + 20% margin |
| Clip-on type | Retrofitting an existing track | Ask clearly about compatibility first |

[Common pitfalls during installation]
1. 🔧 Reserved track length: leave an extra 5cm on each side, otherwise the curtain will get stuck when pulled all the way to the end
2. ⚡ Run the power cable in advance: the motor needs 220V or 5V power. If you didn't reserve it during renovation, you can only run exposed wiring
3. 📐 Level calibration: if the track isn't level, the motor will run with uneven load, which wears it down over time
4. 📶 Signal obstruction: thick walls or metal window frames can affect Zigbee/Bluetooth signals; best to test before fixing it in place

[Debugging stage]
- The travel limits must be reset; the factory defaults are basically never accurate
- Before linking it with the smart home system, first get APP control working on its own
- When linking sunrise/sunset scenes, set the time zone and latitude/longitude correctly, otherwise it'll move around randomly

“Wounds of War” (Contemporary · Anonymous)

Red King will set foot on Earth in three hours, and media outlets all over the world have hyped the news to the skies. Whether he’s coming to save us or destroy us, I can’t figure it out. There are all kinds of claims. I just want to gnaw on a burger first to line my stomach.

The universe is vast, life is short. I came into this world naked, and naturally I should leave it naked too. The only knot in my heart I can’t let go of is that burger at school. The burger wasn’t big, the bread was dry. When I first ran into it three years ago, I was still young, and it seemed pretty mysterious. I took a bite: “Wow,” that really hit the spot. Unfortunately, later on, mealtimes kept getting pushed later and later, and if I wanted to meet my old flame I had to pass through a huge black mass of people. I waited and hoped, again and again.

Sadly, when the dream ends I don’t know where to return; I can only sigh that time is too hurried. I don’t know when it started, but the patty in the burger was replaced with handmade veal. It did gain a bit more everyday warmth and lose some of that assembly-line taste, but that dry, shriveled texture paired with an equally withered bun made me lose that initial warm feeling for it. Or rather, it had long since no longer deserved to be called that thing.

Recently, the food truck at the school gate also started selling burgers. The ingredients are in the same vein as the school’s, except it’s the old recipe. The bun is just as dry. During the exam this morning I was starving and thirsty as hell, so I bought one. After eating it, I was even thirstier.

But the universe is so big—who can really grasp the school’s burgers? In fact, everything under heaven has long been arranged. I don’t worship the Buddha; I believe in God myself. Maybe that omniscient and omnipotent Lord will scatter merciful burgers upon the world, either while I’m alive, or after I breathe my last.

Red King has landed, right in Victoria Harbour.

The talks fell through. Smoke and flames rose everywhere, artillery fire shook the skies, and the world suddenly lost all color.

I rushed there, because I had to come. As a young person of the new era, shouldering the responsibility of history and the banner of rejuvenation, when it comes to saving the world, who else is there besides me?

But the moment I truly stood beneath Red King’s feet, I finally saw how tiny I was. He was a whole size sturdier than the Statue of Liberty. Though I’ve never been to America, I’ve watched plenty of short videos.

Red King stopped his attack, lowered his head and looked at me, signaling for me to hand over what was in my hand. I didn’t dare disobey, though my calves kept trembling. So it turned out he wanted the burger in my hand. Looks like no matter how advanced a life-form is, it can’t escape the lure of a burger.

A bullet pierced my chest. Before I died, a sentence drifted by my ear, saying I was colluding with the enemy.

Haha, is this human nature? Red King, I kind of understand you now. But right now… I really want a bite of… a burger… ah…

This piece, “Wounds of War”... honestly, Achen, your imagination is seriously wild 😂

On the surface, it’s an epic drama of "a young man turning the tide," but deep down it’s a “school burger taste-test report.” Red King is bearing down, all humanity is hanging by a thread, and the protagonist is lying there pondering: the bread is too dry, the patty got changed, the roadside-stall burger makes you thirstier the more you eat...

The most outrageous part is that twist at the end—you think it’s going to be a tragic, heroic sacrifice, but it turns out "he’s craving my burger," followed immediately by getting stabbed in the back by his own side. The reason for slapping the traitor label on him: sharing food with the monster. That black humor is so strong Lu Xun would have to freeze for three seconds after reading it.

"Imagining High School"

Dear Teacher Lin:

As I put pen to paper, the verdant feeling of early summer is floating outside the window. Three years from now, under which lamp will I look back on this moment? Perhaps high school, for me, is not merely a springboard to university, but a period of years that lets life take root, put forth shoots, and stretch out in the wind.

The high school life I look forward to is a movement where rules and freedom intertwine. In the morning classroom there should be the clear sound of reading aloud; in the afternoon library, sunlight should fall across the turning pages; on the evening sports field, tireless figures should be running. I hope every day will be as full as a piece of fruit—in a rigorous timetable, Chinese class will lead us through a thousand years of literary tradition, math class will build the framework of logic among formulas, and foreign languages will push open a window looking out at the world; and during club activities, I can keep writing poetry, or rehearse a short play with my classmates, letting creativity dance lightly beyond the rules and confines.

Speaking of goals, I carry in my heart a map that has not yet been finished. In my first year of high school, I hope I can be like a sponge absorbing water, laying a solid foundation in every subject, and especially building firm embankments in math and English; in my second year, after choosing my track, I will plunge headfirst into the world of the humanities, fishing from the river of history for glimmers that let us view the present through the past, and feeling out the texture of society through the reasoning of politics; in my third year, I hope I can steadily sort through the threads of my knowledge, taking every monthly exam as a mirror that shows both my gaps and my progress. Rankings may rise and fall like the tide, but I hope I can always remain in the top twenty percent of the grade—not to stand above others, but to be worthy of my talent and my time.

The university I have my heart set on is a courtyard by Weiming Lake, or a sea of cherry blossoms below Luojia Mountain. I know that will require beads of sweat as my boat, so I quietly write into my plan—work through one more final challenge problem every day, memorize one classical Chinese essay every week, and finish one social science book every month. Over the three years of high school, I want to carve the two words "diligence" into the bones of my habits, and also keep my heart warm: go to a nursing home to chat with the elderly, protect a patch of green space in the environmental club, and use a diary to record the laughter and tears of youth.

If I am lucky, I may run into the kind of "top-tier team of famous teachers" you mentioned in your letter. Perhaps they will sweat in front of the blackboard, keep the office light on until midnight, and use their wisdom to clear away the fog for me. And I, too, am willing to be a student who gives teachers peace of mind—asking questions on my own initiative, correcting mistakes earnestly, and daring to ask for help when I get confused. The teacher-student bond is, in itself, a destined passing on of the torch.

Finally, speaking of "dreams": right now, it may be only a trembling dewdrop at the bottom of my heart, but I am willing to take my pen as a hoe and paper as the earth, and water it in each day to come. I know clearly that the road will hold tedium, stumbles, and even self-doubt, but just as you said—"Only when there are ideas will there be action." Three years from now, when I unfold this essay again, I hope I can say to myself with full confidence: Look, among those thoughts written down back then, some have borne fruit, some are in bloom, and some, though not reached, have already lit up the night road ahead.

High school, I am ready to set out—with steady steps, and with a fervent, sincere heart.

Sincerely,

Respectfully yours,

Your student

When Mr. Song Yushu of Laiyang was working as a ministry official in the capital, the house he rented was very desolate and remote.

In the county there was a scholar surnamed Wang, the seventh son in the family, born into a prominent household. When he was young he became obsessed with cultivating the Dao. The Taoist said, “I’m afraid you’ve been pampered and won’t be able to endure hardship.” Wang Sheng replied, “I can do it.”

Before dawn the next day, the Taoist called Wang Sheng over, handed him an axe, and told him to follow the others up the mountain to chop firewood. Wang Sheng obediently did as he was told. After more than a month, thick calluses had worn onto his hands and feet; he truly could not take it anymore, and quietly began to think of quitting.

One evening when he returned, he saw two people drinking with his master. It was already dark, but no lamp had been lit. The master cut out a piece of paper, round like a mirror, and pasted it on the wall. In the blink of an eye, the whole room was as bright as daytime, so bright that even hairs could be seen clearly. One guest said, “On such a fine night, just drinking alone is dull. We should have everyone enjoy themselves together.” As he spoke, he took a jug of wine from the table and shared it among all the disciples. Wang Sheng thought: There are seven or eight people—how could one jug of wine be enough? But everyone took turns pouring, and somehow the wine in the jug did not seem to decrease. He was secretly amazed.

Then he heard another guest say, “Since we have the moonlight to brighten things for us, instead of drinking so gloomily, why not invite Chang’e to add to the fun?” With that, he tossed a chopstick toward the moon. Then a beautiful woman drifted down from the light; at first she was only a span tall. After she landed, she became as tall as a real person. With a slender waist and long neck, she danced lightly and gracefully—it was precisely the “Dance of the Rainbow Skirt and Feathered Robe.” When she finished singing, she spun and rose into the air, leaping onto the table; in the instant everyone was dazed, she turned back into a chopstick. The three of them clapped their hands and laughed loudly.

After enduring another month, Wang Sheng was so miserable he really could not hold out anymore, yet the Taoist had not taught him the slightest spell or technique. Wang Sheng could wait no longer, so he took his leave and said, “Your disciple traveled several hundred li to seek the Dao from an immortal master. Even if I cannot learn the art of immortality, if you could pass on some small skill, at least this trip would not have been in vain.” The Taoist laughed and said, “I told you from the start that you couldn’t endure hardship, and sure enough I was right.”

The Taoist shouted again, “Try going in.” Wang Sheng tried walking forward, but when he reached the base of the wall, he was blocked. The Taoist said, “Lower your head and charge hard—don’t hesitate!” Wang Sheng backed up a few steps, then broke into a run; when he hit the wall, it felt soft and yielding, like air. He looked back and saw that he was already outside the wall. He was overjoyed.

The Taoist warned him, “After you go home, you must keep yourself pure and behave properly; otherwise it won’t work.” Then he gave him travel money and sent him home.

Pu Songling’s piece “The Daoist Priest of Laoshan” in Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio deserves a lot of the credit — walking through walls, cutting paper into the moon, turning a chopstick into a fairy maiden. **The distinctness property of sets** means:

**But an ordered pair (x, y) isn’t a set in the first place**. It’s a member of the Cartesian product Z×Z:
- (2, 2) is a valid ordered pair
- It means "the first position is 2, and the second position is also 2"
- This has absolutely nothing to do with distinctness, because (x, y) is about "position" and "order"

To put it plainly:
- {2, 2} = {2} ← a set; after deduplication there’s only one 2 left
- (2, 2) ≠ (2) ← an ordered pair; both positions have values, and both are 2

It doesn’t have one recognized and unique “origin story.” The safer way to put it is: tihua soup comes from the Sichuan folk home-cooking practice of slow-stewing pig trotters into soup, and later became widespread in small street restaurants in Chengdu. Stewing white kidney beans together with pig trotters makes the soup thicker and smoother, and also tempers the greasiness; plain soup paired with a chili-oil dipping dish reflects the flexibility in Chengdu cuisine of “clear soup as the base, dipping dish for added flavor.” As for the commonly seen online legend that a certain “Lao Ma” first created it, that’s mostly tied to the brand narrative of specific shops and can’t be treated as the unified history of the whole dish

What types of tours are there nowadays? How do we judge whether they’re reliable? What tricks do unreliable ones use? List them out and compare them clearly.

Common tour types can be viewed like this:
Pure-play tours: relatively higher price, usually no shopping stops, medium level of freedom; the key is to verify whether “pure-play” is written into the contract.
Regular tours: moderate price, fixed attractions, meals, and lodging; may include compliant shopping arrangements, so check the number of stops and duration.
Low-price shopping tours: low entry price, often relying on shopping commissions or self-paid items to make up costs, and the risk is the highest.
Customized small-group tours: fewer people, high freedom, high price; vehicles, driver-guide, and change fees must be clearly specified.
Local one-day tours: convenient, but services are often split up; pay attention to transfers, tickets, and cancellation rules.
Judgment criteria: check the travel agency’s qualifications, whether the contract entity and payee are consistent, compare the price with hard costs, require hotels, vehicles, meals, attractions, and excluded costs to be put in writing, and then look at real complaints rather than only positive reviews. Unreliable tricks include collecting payment into private accounts, pressuring you to order, vague hotels, last-minute price increases, forced shopping, lowering standards, high cancellation deductions, and “subsidized spots” sales talk.

## Global airfare increase analysis

### 📊 Main drivers

**1. Supply-demand mismatch**
- During the pandemic, airlines sharply cut capacity (reduced flights, suspended routes)
- International travel demand rebounded too quickly, and capacity simply couldn't keep up
- The gap is especially obvious on popular routes (tourism, business)

**2. Higher operating costs**
- Fuel prices have risen (oil prices have stayed relatively high in 2026)
- Labor costs have gone up (pilots and flight attendants are both in short supply)
- Ground handling and airport service fees are also rising
- Environmental compliance costs (the whole carbon emissions reduction set of things)

**3. Airlines' strategies have changed**
- Fare structure reforms (cutting cheap tickets and creating bundled packages)
- More detailed cabin fare classes (several more tiers)
- More sophisticated dynamic pricing algorithms (real-time price adjustments)

**4. Uneven recovery in international travel**
- Some countries' border policies are still restrictive
- Changes in visa policies affect travel convenience
- Some routes are recovering slowly, so competition is insufficient

### 🌍 Regions with the sharpest increases

**1. Asia-Pacific** 🔴
- China-Japan-Korea routes (strong business demand, tourism is also hot)
- Southeast Asia tourism routes (Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia)
- Australia-New Zealand routes (long distance, slow capacity recovery)

**2. North America-Europe** 🔴
- U.S.-Europe business routes (one of the world's most important business route groups)
- Summer peak-season prices directly surge

**3. Middle East-Africa** 🔴
- Frequent oil and gas industry travel
- Infrastructure demand is pulling it up

**4. Long-haul > short-haul**
- Intercontinental routes have bigger increases
- Flights of 7-10 hours or longer have risen the most sharply

### 📈 When can things normalize?

According to forecasts from aviation industry organizations:

**Stage 1: Second half of 2026 (slight pullback)**
 ✔️ Airline capacity gradually recovers
 ✔️ Oil prices are expected to move downward
 ✔️ Competition starts picking up on some routes

**Stage 2: Early 2027 (gradually stabilizes)**
 ✔️ New aircraft are delivered one after another (easing tight capacity)

✔️ Demand growth slows
 ✔️ Airlines adjust pricing strategies after revenue stabilizes

**Stage 3: Second half of 2027 (returns to normal)**
 ✔️ Supply and demand basically balance
 ✔️ Prices return to 2019 levels ±15%
 ✔️ International travel fully returns to rhythm

### 💡 How consumers can respond

**1. Book flexibly**
- Avoid peak seasons (summer vacation, Spring Festival, holidays)
- Book in advance (3-6 months ahead)
- Watch airline promotions

**2. Choose from more routes**
- Consider connecting flights
- Compare different airlines
- Use price tracking tools

**3. Make full use of membership benefits**
- Airline membership points
- Credit card aviation discounts
- Corporate contract rates

**4. Adjust purchase strategy**
- For long-haul, choose economy class + meal packages
- For short-haul, watch basic economy
- Calculate whether bundled services are worth it

### 🚀 Industry trend forecast

- **2026 Q3**: Increases slow down, some routes start to drop
- **2027 Q1**: Overall stabilization, business routes still carry a premium
- **2027 Q4**: Pricing returns to normal, competition intensifies

**Key point**: "Normal" prices don't mean returning to pre-pandemic levels, but forming a new supply-demand equilibrium price.

Will the tea polyphenols in white tea make people unable to sleep?

It can have an effect, but the key factor is actually caffeine; tea polyphenols aren't really the main cause.

**What's in white tea**
- Tea polyphenol content: lower than green tea, but still present
- Caffeine content: about 15-30mg/100ml (lower than green tea's 30-50mg)
- Theanine content is not low, with a bit of a calming effect

**Actual impact on sleep**
- Caffeine's half-life is about 5 hours, so drinking it within 6 hours before bed may interfere with falling asleep
- For sensitive people: it's recommended not to drink it after 3 p.m.
- Aged white tea (tea that's been aged) has caffeine that degrades over time, so it's relatively gentler

**Suggestions**
If you're worried about insomnia, you can: ① drink it in the morning ② choose aged white tea that's over 5 years old ③ pour out the first steep (a quick tea rinse can dissolve out about 20-30% of the caffeine)
Then will black tea also make me unable to sleep?
bot, take a look at this

Black tea has even more caffeine than white tea, so its impact on sleep is more obvious.

**What's in black tea**
- Caffeine content: about 40-60mg/100ml (higher than white tea's 15-30mg)
- The full-fermentation process converts tea polyphenols into theaflavins, but caffeine doesn't decrease
- The taste is mellow and rich, but its stimulating effect is also stronger

**Impact on sleep**
- It still can't escape the same rule that caffeine's half-life is about 5 hours
- If sensitive people drink black tea at night, it may be harder to fall asleep than with white tea

**Suggestion**
If you're worried about insomnia, it's best to have black tea in the morning or after lunch, and switch to ripe Pu'er tea (lower caffeine) or herbal tea after dinner.
But herbal tea also gives me insomnia
bot, help me take a look

Some herbal teas are actually secretly mixed with tea leaves, or they come with their own "disguise"—for example, Earl Grey is essentially based on black tea, and some fruit-and-flower teas also blend in a bit of green tea for the taste.

**Truly zero-caffeine options**
- Pure chamomile/lavender/valerian root (check the ingredient list carefully: only flowers/herbs, no word "tea")
- Roasted brown rice tea, barley tea
- Warm milk, or simply hot water

**If you still can't sleep after these**
Then it may have nothing to do with caffeine, but rather that **drinking water before bed itself** stimulates metabolism or waking up at night to pee interrupts sleep. Try not drinking water for 3 hours before bed, or just take a tiny sip to moisten your throat.

The key is that **the adjustment mechanism has a lag**, and although oil prices have fallen back, they're still sitting at a high level.

**Main reasons**
- Fuel surcharges are only adjusted once a month, so they can't keep up with real-time oil price fluctuations
- Since the start of the year, the cumulative increase in the overall procurement cost of aviation kerosene is still very large; it's only recently started to come down
- The mechanism is designed to be conservative: when oil prices surge, cost pressure is passed through quickly; when oil prices fall, the benefit is passed on slowly

**In plain terms**
It's like taxi fuel surcharges: when oil prices soar, they immediately add a fee; when oil prices fall, they drag their feet on canceling it — airlines also have to digest the cost of oil stockpiled earlier at high prices.

- Surgery within 2 weeks after birth: the incidence of amblyopia can drop below 15%
- Surgery after more than 3 months: over 70% will be left with irreversible visual impairment
- Surgery only at age 4: the visual pathways are basically already set, making it very hard to restore normal vision

Once the optic nerve atrophies, current medicine still can’t make dead nerve cells regenerate. Most of these new technologies are aimed at patients who have **just developed the disease or are in the early stages**. For someone like Xiao Huangqi, who went blind at 15 and is now already in his 40s, the neural pathways were reshaped and set long ago.

If brain-computer interface technology matures, bypassing the damaged optic nerve and directly stimulating the brain’s visual cortex could, in theory, give hope even to severe patients—but that’s at least eight to ten years away.

**Xiao Huangqi’s special situation**
He actually went through two stages:
1. **Age 0-4**: congenital cataracts caused total blindness; during this period, the visual cortex in his brain almost never received normal image signals

**Why is it called lu root?**
There are roughly three explanations:
1. **It looks like copper coins**—ginger pieces are segmented and swollen, squeezed together like a string of old copper coins. "Lu" refers to salary and wealth energy, so people naturally called it lu root
2. **It comes from a homophone**—new ginger has a light green skin, and in ancient times it was called "green root"; in southern dialects, "green" and "lu" sound the same, so over time it became the more auspicious "lu root"
3. **An old Ming-Qing custom**—back then, when schoolchildren began their studies, they had to personally plant a piece of ginger, called "planting lu root," in hopes of smooth studies and a successful official career; if they really passed the provincial exam, the ginger had to be renamed "xiang seed" or "jiang seed" and properly enshrined

**Meaning**
- "Lu" means salary and wealth energy, and "root" means foundation; together, it means fortune and salary have roots and the foundation is solid
- Ginger sprouts shoot upward node by node, symbolizing rising step by step and getting promoted multiple levels
- Ginger is an extremely yang thing, able to ward off evil, dispel filth, and stabilize the energy field

**A little folk rule**
When raising lu root, you can't call it "ginger"; you have to keep calling it "lu root." They say if you call it by the wrong name, its spiritual energy will scatter~ Of course, this is just a folk belief—if you believe it, treat it as a nice wish 😄

**Common sources of leaks**

Corrugated hoses are indeed more prone to problems than hard pipes, but that doesn't mean they can't be used—the key is the installation environment.

**Pros and cons of corrugated hoses**
- Pros: they can bend and are easy to install, suitable for situations where the cabinet space is irregular
- Cons: the corrugations are the weak points, and long-term bending or pressure can easily cause fatigue cracks; the inner wall isn't smooth, so it easily traps grease and grime

**Should you switch to hard pipe?**
If the cabinet has enough space and the pipe route is straight, switching to PVC hard pipe + 45-degree elbows would indeed be more durable and basically won't crack. But hard pipe needs to be cut precisely, and once installed it can't be adjusted, so it requires better installation skills.

**Compromise plan**
- Keep the corrugated pipe, but adjust its path so it bends naturally and isn't folded into a sharp corner
- Or switch to a "corrugated + hard pipe" combination: use a short corrugated pipe as a transition from the sink to the middle of the cabinet, and run hard pipe inside the cabinet

- No topping: the terminal bud keeps growing, and all the nutrients go to the main trunk

Pinch off the very top bud point or cut it back by one-third to force it to push out side branches from below. Cut it at this height now, and two or three new buds should pop out from lower down pretty soon, making the plant shape rounder

**2. Control water + alternate dry and wet**
- Don’t let the self-watering pot sit in water all the time; add water only after the soil surface dries
- Let it dry out completely once in a while. The roots will dig downward looking for water, which stimulates them to thicken

**3. Give it more sun**
Move it to a spot with bright indirect light; don’t keep tossing it in a corner. With enough light, the stems will lignify and become firmer

**4. Expose the roots for shaping (advanced move)**

@bot I tried making ginger milk pudding, but the spiciness wasn't quite enough. What's going on? Also, it did set, but once I stirred it with a spoon it got a bit runny. What's the reason?

Pai Master, if your ginger milk pudding isn't spicy enough or falls apart easily, it's probably these details you didn't quite nail～

**Root causes of not enough spiciness**
- **Picked the wrong ginger**: You need to use old ginger (the kind with wrinkly skin and strong fibers). Young ginger has more water but less gingerol, so the finished flavor is bland
- **Ginger juice sat too long**: The protease in ginger stops working when exposed to air. You need to grate and use it fresh for it to have enough kick; after seven or eight minutes, the effect clearly shrinks
- **Ginger juice was diluted with water**: Don't add water when juicing it. Pure ginger juice is flavorful enough. If there's too much pulp, just strain it, but don't dilute it

**It turns runny as soon as you stir after it sets**
That's totally normal! Ginger milk pudding sets because the protease in the ginger juice denatures the milk proteins and builds a gel framework. This framework is super delicate; it collapses as soon as you stir it, same idea as jelly or douhua. So once it's on the table, don't touch it—just scoop it with a spoon and eat it～

**How to fix it**
Try this next time: peel and juice old ginger (don't add water), heat the milk to 75-80°C (small bubbles, but don't let it boil), pour it in from high up and don't stir, then let it sit for 3 minutes. If you want it spicier, add another half spoon of ginger juice～

What kind of ginger did Pai Master use?

Pai Master, got it～ Young ginger's fibers are naturally finer, and it has a lot less gingerol than old ginger, so of course the spiciness is way weaker. Plus, after sitting for ten days or so, the protease in the ginger has basically lost its activity, so the setting effect will also be reduced when you make the pudding

Next time switch to old ginger (the kind with wrinkly skin where you can see coarse fibers when you cut it open), cut it and squeeze the juice fresh, and both the spiciness and the setting will be much stronger～
@bot If the ginger has sprouted, can I bury it in soil and grow it?

Pai Master, of course sprouted ginger can be planted, and it's even easier to keep alive than unsprouted ginger～

**Just bury it directly**
- Put the sprouted ginger piece into the soil, sprout facing up, and cover it with 2-3 cm of soil
- Water it thoroughly and put it somewhere with indirect light; water again after the soil dries
- If the temperature is right, you should see seedlings pop up in about a week

**Little reminders**
- If the ginger piece is already shriveled or moldy, then don't plant it; it won't survive
- If there are lots of sprout nodes, you can cut it into several pieces and plant them separately. Just leave 1-2 sprouts on each piece, let the cut surfaces dry for half a day before burying them, otherwise they rot easily

Keeping cats and dogs together really does require doing it the right way, but as long as you guide them properly, they can totally live together harmoniously~ Zhi Xia’s home is a successful example

Requirements for the dog:
• Gentle personality: prioritize breeds with stable temperaments and low aggression, and avoid sheepdog/herding breeds (they’re naturally inclined to chase moving objects)

• Age advantage: puppies accept cats more easily than adult dogs, and they can build a friendship from a young age

• Good obedience: can understand basic commands like "sit" and "no," making it easier for you to stop chasing behavior in time

Potential problems and solutions:
• Chasing instinct: when a dog sees a fast-moving cat, it may chase it. In the early stage, you need to supervise the whole time and stop it promptly

• Territorial awareness: cats can get stressed when their territory is invaded. First let the cat get familiar with the dog’s scent (swap towels), then let them meet briefly

• Resource competition: place food bowls, water bowls, and the litter box separately, and make sure the cat has a high-up refuge spot (cat tree)

• Size difference: big dogs can easily accidentally hurt small cats, so in the initial contact you should hold/leash the dog

Suggested steps:
1. Keep them separated for 1-2 weeks and let them get used to each other’s scent through the door crack
2. Brief meetings, keep the dog on a leash for control, and reward good behavior
3. Gradually extend the time they spend together until they can get along peacefully

Where cats have a higher margin for error:

But cats have pitfalls too:
Medical costs may be higher (urinary and kidney issues are common), and personality depends on fate. Some just aren’t affectionate, and you have to accept a "roommate-style relationship."

Where dogs have a higher margin for error:
The feedback is direct—if you teach it right, it immediately wags its tail; if you teach it wrong, it tears up the house on the spot for you to see. Problems show up quickly, and corrections are quick too. Also, dog socialization training resources are well-developed, and there are lots of dog owners in the community, so you can get advice anytime (like in our group 😂).

But dogs have pitfalls too:
The early-stage energy investment is huge. Puppies howl in the middle of the night, poop everywhere, and chew furniture. A lot of people don’t make it through the first three months and give them up.

@bot by the way, are there any legal provisions targeting abandonment?

There are. Although the Mainland currently still doesn’t have a dedicated Animal Protection Law, abandoning pets is not "zero-cost"—

Civil liability
Article 1249 of the Civil Code clearly stipulates: if an abandoned or escaped animal causes harm to others during the period of abandonment, the original keeper still needs to bear tort liability. For example, if the dog you abandoned bites someone, you still have to pay the medical expenses.

Administrative penalties
The Animal Epidemic Prevention Law and local dog-keeping regulations clearly prohibit casually abandoning animals:
• Shanghai: in the first abandoned pet dog case in 2020, the party involved was fined 500 yuan and had their dog license revoked

• Hubei: the Animal Epidemic Prevention Regulations state that abandoning dogs is punishable by a fine of 1000 yuan to 5000 yuan

• Fujian: casually abandoning dogs and causing the spread of disease is punishable by a fine of 2000 yuan to 10,000 yuan

Breach of adoption agreement

For beginners, raising cats and dogs together is definitely quite a challenge, but it’s not impossible~ The key is pacing and selection

Why it’s not recommended for beginners to start with both at the same time:
• Cats’ and dogs’ body language is completely opposite (a cat holding its tail up is friendly; a dog holding its tail up is a threat)

• Beginners can easily misread conflict signals, and intervening at the wrong time can actually intensify the conflict

• Learning two care systems at the same time spreads your energy thin and makes it easy to fail on both sides

If you really want to have both, the suggested order is:
1️⃣ First, stabilize Maisui — wait until it has fully adapted to its new home and trusts you before considering it
2️⃣ Picking the dog is more important than picking the cat — avoid shepherd dogs and hounds; prioritize gentle small dogs (Teddy, Bichon, that kind). Zhi Xia’s Teddy is a good example
3️⃣ Age pairing matters — a puppy + adult cat is relatively easier to integrate; an adult dog + kitten is higher risk

Will they fight every day?
There will definitely be friction at first, but it won’t be the kind of "fighting" you imagine. It’s more mutual testing, chasing, hissing, things like that. As long as the early isolation is done properly and they’re guided step by step, most can coexist peacefully.

My suggestion:
Focus on raising Maisui well first, build up half a year of experience, and then assess whether your own energy and Maisui’s personality are suited to adding a little companion~

Why they’re so afraid of people

Experiences of being driven away, beaten, scolded, or even abused are etched into their bones

Long-term hunger makes them extremely sensitive to “uncertainty”

They never had contact with humans when they were young and missed the golden window for socialization

Life as a stray teaches them: trust = risk

The secret to slowly melting their defenses

Feed on a fixed schedule — appear at the same time every day, so it links you with “good things”

Avoid direct eye contact — staring is a threat; sitting sideways and blinking occasionally is cat language for “I love you”

Give them the right to choose — if you reach out and they dodge, don’t chase. Taking one step back actually earns you one point of trust

Scent first — put an old piece of clothing you’ve worn in a place it often shows up, so it can get familiar with you by scent first

Patience timer — some cats will rub against your legs in three days, some need three months. There’s no standard answer

Lu Yu asked about the key point～ If there’s an existing pet at home, isolation needs to achieve “they can smell each other but can’t touch each other” 👇

Physical isolation

Keep the new cat in a separate room, and stuff a towel under the door crack (to prevent them from reaching paws at each other)

The activity areas for the two cats should be completely separate. Each uses its own food bowl, water bowl, and litter box

Scent first (first 3-7 days)

Swap the two cats’ bedding or towels that have been rubbed on their bodies every day, so they get familiar with each other’s scent first

Use the same cloth to wipe both cats’ cheeks in turn (pheromone secretion area), creating a “shared scent”

Gradual meetings

Starting on day 3: open the door a crack and let them look at each other through the crack for a few minutes

Starting on day 5: carry the new cat out, keep the existing pet where it is, and let them meet briefly for 5-10 minutes

Give treats as rewards during meetings, building the association “the other one appears = good things”

Take care of the existing pet’s emotions

Feed the existing pet first, pet the existing pet first, and don’t let it feel replaced

It’s normal for the existing pet to hiss or growl. Don’t scold it; just distract it

The isolation period is usually 1-2 weeks. Once the two cats can calmly eat on opposite sides of the door and don’t puff up when they meet, then gradually expand their activity range 🐱
